note: Diverse perspectives on trafficking, scams, and online safety from researchers, survivors, and practitioners

voices.name: Carolina Morón
voices.quote: Most people don't realize that trafficking starts with an offer that sounds too good to be true—but also sounds just real enough. The vibe check is about trusting your intuition when something doesn't add up.
voices.bio: Carolina leads research on how technology amplifies exploitation risks and how design can empower people to protect themselves.

voices.name: Labour Trafficking Researcher
voices.quote: H-2A visa trafficking happens because the system is designed to trap workers. Once you're in the country, you owe fees, your documents are taken, and you can't leave. The warning signs are there from day one—if you know what to look for.
voices.bio: Researches visa-based labor trafficking and structural exploitation patterns.

voices.name: Sex Trafficking Prevention
voices.quote: Online grooming rarely starts with explicit harm. It starts with isolation: 'your family won't understand us,' 'keep this between us.' When someone asks you to hide the relationship, that's your signal to pause and check the vibe.
voices.bio: Focuses on online safety and preventing grooming through awareness and support.

voices.name: Romance Scam Analyst
voices.quote: Romance scammers move fast: 'my camera is broken' (no video verification), 'I love you already' (artificial urgency), 'my uncle has a crypto opportunity' (pivot to money). Each step is designed to lower your guard incrementally.
voices.bio: Analyzes romance scam tactics and their psychological manipulation strategies.

voices.name: Data Scientist
voices.quote: The CTDC dataset shows 206,000 cases with clear patterns: recruitment promises are rarely held. Job offers with visa sponsorship, 'free' housing, or rapid promotion are flagged in over 70% of documented trafficking cases. These aren't coincidences—they're intentional lures.
voices.bio: Uses data analysis to identify patterns in trafficking and exploitation cases.

voices.name: Anti-Trafficking Lawyer
voices.quote: Survivors often say, 'I didn't realize it was a trap until I was already in it.' By then, they've lost money, documents, or been isolated from their network. Vibe Check is about catching the trap *before* you step into it.
voices.bio: Brings legal expertise on survivor support and policy solutions.

survivors.name: Kayla
survivors.quote: It started with someone who seemed to care about me. They isolated me from my family and friends, and before I realized what was happening, I was trapped.
survivors.bio: Kayla's story illustrates how trafficking often begins with exploitation of emotional vulnerabilities and trust, leading to isolation and loss of autonomy.

survivors.name: Celine
survivors.quote: I was promised good wages and housing. When I arrived, my documents were taken and I owed so much money for travel that I could never leave.
survivors.bio: Celine's experience shows the common trafficking pattern: false promises, document confiscation, and debt bondage that traps workers.

survivors.name: Omar
survivors.quote: I was taken from school to work in the mine. It was dangerous and I had no choice. My family was desperate and I was sold.
survivors.bio: Omar's account reveals how poverty and family desperation create vulnerabilities that traffickers exploit, particularly affecting children.

survivors.name: Samiya
survivors.quote: I was just a child working in the factory instead of going to school. The conditions were unsafe and the pay was nothing.
survivors.bio: Samiya's story highlights child labor in manufacturing, where children are exploited for their economic value in dangerous conditions.
